thread.title: New products let bulls and bears make turbocharged bets on tech

author: Ryan Vlastelica
title: New products let bulls and bears make turbocharged bets on tech
text:
Investors who want to continue playing one of 2017’s hottest trades can now do so in turbocharged fashion.
A pair of exchange-traded notes will debut on Tuesday that offer triple-leveraged exposure to large-capitalization technology and internet names, a group that drove a hefty percentage of the overall market’s gain in 2017, albeit with heavy volatility.
The BMO REX MicroSectors FANG+ Index 3X Leveraged ETN FNGU, -0.19% tracks an index of 10 stocks, returning 300% of the index’s daily move. What this means is that on an day when the index rises 1%, the ETN is designed to rise 3%.
While leveraged products are designed to deliver outsize moves on a day-to-day basis, most analysts agree they are primarily designed and better suited to professional traders, given their inherent volatility, increased riskiness, higher fees, and their use as a short-term holding.
Another fund, the BMO REX MicroSectors FANG+ Index -3X Inverse Leveraged ETN FNGD, -0.08% is an inverse leveraged note on the same theme. One a day when the underlying index rises 1%, this fund should fall 3%. It is a way for investors to make an outsize bet on the idea that the stocks—which many analysts have claimed are highly overvalued following their gargantuan 2017 gains—are due for a setback.
The term “FANG” refers to the so-called FANG stocks, or four names that emerged as trading favorites last year: Facebook FB, +1.01% Amazon AMZN, +1.30% Netflix NFLX, +9.99% and Google parent Alphabet GOOGL, +0.53% The ETNs hold those four, along with six other stocks, including: Apple AAPL, +0.66% Nvidia NVDA, +1.22% Tesla TSLA, +0.76% Twitter TWTR, -3.15% and two stocks from China—Alibaba BABA, +1.76% and Baidu BIDU, -0.36% 
All 10 of those stocks are sharply higher over the past 12 months, easily outperforming the 25% rise of the S&P 500 SPX, -0.03% over the same period. Alphabet is the relative runt of the litter, having gained only 37.9% over the period, while Nvidia has more than doubled. Amazon, Netflix, and Alibaba have all gained more than 60%, and Netflix extended that move on Tuesday, rallying a day after its quarterly results.
